question: What portion of Uber’s 2024 revenue growth was driven by take-rate expansion versus volume growth?
answer:
Take Rate:
2023: 27.04%
2024: 27.02%

Take rate was virtually flat from 2023 to 2024. Overall revenue growth was 18%, driven by the 18% gross bookings growth YoY (25% in mobility, 17% in delivery and 2% in freight). Hence, all growth in revenue was driven by pure volume as opposed to take rate increases

model_answer:
**Short answer: essentially none.** On a reported basis, Uber’s 2024 revenue growth was driven by volume/Gross Bookings growth; take rate was flat to slightly down.

| FY2024 vs. FY2023 | 2023 | 2024 | Change |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Revenue | $37.281B | $43.978B | **+17.96%** |
| Gross Bookings | $137.865B | $162.773B | **+18.07%** |
| Revenue margin / take rate | 27.04% | 27.02% | **-2.4 bps** |

Using **Revenue = Gross Bookings × take rate**:

- **Volume contribution:** **+18.07 pp**
- **Take-rate contribution:** **-0.09 pp**
- **Interaction:** **-0.02 pp**
- **Total revenue growth:** **+17.96%**

In dollar terms, the **+$6.70B** revenue increase comprised roughly **+$6.74B from Gross Bookings growth** at the prior-year take rate, offset by about **-$0.04B from lower take rate/mix**. So volume explains slightly more than 100% of reported growth, while take-rate expansion explains none—it was a small drag.

**Important nuance:** Segment trends were mixed. Mobility’s full-year revenue margin expanded from ~28.8% to ~30.2% (+~140 bps), while Delivery’s fell from ~19.1% to ~18.4% (~-70 bps). Combined Mobility + Delivery margin rose ~50 bps, but Freight’s shrinking share—where revenue is roughly 100% of Gross Bookings—held the total-company margin flat. Also, reported 2024 revenue was reduced by **$1.58B** from business-model/contra-revenue changes ($863M Mobility, $713M Delivery). Adding that back, adjusted revenue growth would be ~22.2%, with volume still contributing ~18.1 pp (~81%) and take-rate/mix ~4.1 pp (~19%). But on the reported result: **all growth came from volume, not take-rate expansion.**

Sources: [Uber Q4/FY2024 release](https://investor.uber.com/news-events/news/press-release-details/2025/Uber-Announces-Results-for-Fourth-Quarter-and-Full-Year-2024/default.aspx); [Uber 2024 Form 10-K](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1543151/000154315125000008/uber-20241231.htm).
judge_reason: Main total take-rate, flat, revenue, bookings, and volume-driven growth checks are met, but the mobility, delivery, and freight segment growth figures are omitted.
